Phase 49: legacy skill drift — plan submission (round 1). docs/phases/legacy-skill-drift.md on branch phase-49-legacy-skill-drift.

Three post-Phase-48 findings: (1) ten user-level ~/.claude/skills/handoff-* skills from the pre-plugin era (0 hits for gatekeeper|GATE_BOUNCE|interject|AMEND each; the plugin contract has 8) competed with tagteam:handoff in every project — removed by hand on the arbiter's machine today, backed up; (2) tagteam/data/workflows.md, copied into every project by setup/upgrade, documents the dead /handoff-* command family (re-copied into 29 projects during today's sweep); (3) server.py:1435 emits `/handoff-cycle {phase}`.

(2) and (3) are drift and are fixed in scope. (1) is the design question the arbiter referred to this cycle: should a project tool touch ~/.claude at all? Options A (nothing) / B (detect and report from setup/upgrade, never delete) / C (remove). Lead recommends B on the Phase 48 provenance rule — setup may only delete what setup wrote, and it never wrote those directories. Please rule on A/B/C; if C, scope grows by an explicit --remove-superseded flag, never default. Everything else (detection function, one-note-per-run, workflows.md rewrite to the 3.10 surface, audit test extended to shipped data/*.md, "Done means", verification) is in the doc.

Ruling: Option B — detect and report only. Do not add deletion behavior or a removal flag in this phase.

Required plan changes:

1. Treat filename matches as candidates, not proven superseded artifacts. A user-owned handoff or handoff-* directory may be custom, so rename the helper and warning accordingly (for example legacy_handoff_skill_candidates / potentially conflicting user-level skills). The current claim that detection is exact is unsupported without provenance or content validation.

2. Do not print a ready-to-run recursive rm command for global user configuration. Report the resolved paths, state that tagteam did not modify them, and tell the user to review and remove confirmed legacy copies manually. This avoids unsafe shell interpolation, shell-specific brace expansion, and accidental deletion of a custom skill.

3. Specify config-root resolution accurately. plugin_status currently delegates discovery to the Claude CLI; it does not itself implement CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR path resolution. Add a dedicated, tested resolver for the read-only scan, including unset and overridden cases.

4. Make the once-per-run behavior concrete: setup may report once, while upgrade must suppress per-project setup reporting and emit one aggregate/global note. Test a multi-project upgrade, not only a single project.

Retain the planned workflows.md rewrite, project-aware server command, recursive shipped-doc/runtime audit, and no session-start-hook change. With these revisions, the scope is appropriate.

Round 2 — ruling B taken as given (no deletion, no flag; "Out" now says so). All four changes applied, tagged (r2) in docs/phases/legacy-skill-drift.md.

1. Candidates, not proven: helper renamed legacy_handoff_skill_candidates(config_dir=None) -> list[Path]; the doc now states a name match is a candidate only (tagteam has no provenance for these — it never shipped them) and withdraws the "detection is exact" claim. Note wording: "N user-level skill(s) under <config>/skills may conflict with the tagteam plugin's /tagteam:handoff".
2. No shell command: the note lists resolved paths, says "tagteam did not modify them. Review each; remove confirmed pre-plugin copies yourself." Test asserts no `rm` token anywhere in the output and that candidates are byte-identical afterwards.
3. Config-root resolution: dedicated tested claude_config_dir() — $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR when set and non-empty (expanded; need not exist), else ~/.claude; unset / set / empty cases tested. Corrected the round-1 misstatement that plugin_status resolves this itself (it delegates to the Claude CLI).
4. Once per run, concretely: setup.main(project, report_user_skills=True) is the default (setup / quickstart report once per invocation); upgrade passes report_user_skills=False per project and prints one aggregate note at the end. Test: upgrade over three registered projects → the note appears exactly once in the whole output and not inside any per-project block.

Retained unchanged: workflows.md rewrite to the 3.10 surface, project-aware server command, recursive audit (now explicitly tagteam/data/**/*.md + tagteam/**/*.py), no session-start-hook change.

The Round 1 requirements are addressed, but two internal contradictions remain in the plan.

1. The candidate helper promises both resolved (realpath) directories and symlinked entries reported by their link path. Path.resolve/realpath dereferences the link, so both cannot be true. Preserve and report the absolute lexical candidate path under <config>/skills (including the symlink path), and do not realpath the candidate itself. State separately how the config root is expanded/absolutized. Add a test where the symlink target is outside the config directory so the asserted output makes the intended boundary unambiguous.

2. The Option B table still says the report names one command to run, contradicting the ruled design that emits no shell command. Update that cell to say it names the candidate paths and manual review action.

Everything else in Round 2 is acceptable. This is a plan-only consistency fix; no broader scope change is requested.

Round 3 — the two consistency fixes, tagged (r3).

1. Path reporting made unambiguous: the config root is expanded and absolutized lexically once (expanduser().absolute(), no symlink dereference); each candidate is reported as <root>/skills/<name> — the absolute lexical path, never realpath'd — so a symlinked entry is reported by its link path under the config dir, not its target. The contradictory "resolved (realpath)" wording is gone. Test added: a symlinked entry whose target lies outside the config dir is reported exactly once as <config>/skills/<name> and the outside target path never appears in the output; a relative or ~-prefixed CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR yields absolute reported paths.
2. Option B table cell now says the report names the candidate paths and the manual review action, and that no shell command is emitted — consistent with the ruling.

No other changes.

Approved. Option B is fully specified: read-only candidate reporting, no deletion behavior or generated shell command, dedicated lexical config-root resolution, symlink candidates reported by their in-config link paths, once-per-run setup and upgrade behavior, current workflow/runtime strings, and focused verification. The Round 3 corrections remove the remaining contradictions.
